items.title: A power torsion module is unchanged by base change along a map that is an isomorphism on the quotients by the powers of the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that if a ring map induces isomorphisms on the quotients by all powers of an ideal, then the base change of any power torsion module along that map is an isomorphism, and identifies the case of the completion of a finitely generated ideal as a special case (statement lines 24172-24183). The proof is a two-stage computation: for a module annihilated by a fixed power the base change is identified with the tensor product over the quotient against the base changed quotient and hence with the module itself, and an arbitrary power torsion module is written as the union of those submodules so that the statement follows from commutation of the tensor product with direct limits (proof lines 24185-24198). The identification over the quotient is what makes the fixed power case immediate. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed.
